jobs.description:
Staff Software Engineer - Databases SRE | UK | Remote

Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a remote opportunity and we are looking for candidates from the UK, Sweden, Spain or Germany.

About the role:

Grafana Cloud runs Mimir, Loki, Tempo and Pyroscope as multi-tenant SaaS databases across AWS, GCP and Azure in regions worldwide. Our highest-SLA customers depend on them to run their businesses. We’re looking for a Staff Software Engineer to keep these systems reliable at scale.

The role combines building and operating. You’ll write the software, automation and product changes that make our databases more reliable, including changes to the Mimir, Loki and Tempo codebases where reliability calls for it. You’ll also be on call for our highest-SLA customers and handle the operational work that comes with it. You’ll bring a production mindset to product engineering and engineering rigor to reliability, and you’ll set technical direction across squads.

What You’ll Do

  • Build reliability into the product. Write production code in our services, tooling and the Mimir, Loki and Tempo codebases that makes our databases more resilient, self-healing and scalable as demand grows quickly.
  • Build automation and platform tooling that removes toil and scales our reliability practices across regions and cloud providers.
  • Lead technical design. Author design docs, review others’ designs and PRs, and shape feature design so it’s scalable and operable from day one.
  • Own the SLO framework. Define and evolve per-tenant SLOs and reliability models. Use SLO burn and incident learnings to find and fix the causes of failure in the systems themselves.
  • Improve observability and alerting so we find problems before customers do, and so escalations are actionable rather than noisy.
  • Be on call for our highest-SLA customers. Act as a technical escalation point for complex customer environments. Lead customer-impacting incident response, including customer bridge calls when needed, and write blameless post-incident reviews that lead to engineering fixes.
  • Handle the operational work that comes from on-call. This includes investigating customer escalations, following up on incident actions, tuning capacity and configuration, and turning recurring issues into permanent fixes or automation.
  • Multiply the team. Mentor engineers, teach reliability practices that teams adopt early in development, and work with engineering leadership on roadmaps and product strategy.
  • We highly value those who are intellectually curious, who default to transparency, possess a high bias towards action, and who are also kind (this is important!)

On-Call

Weekday on-call is 12-hour shifts, Monday to Friday, split between North America and Europe so you cover your local working hours. Weekends are covered by a separate 24-hour rotation. You’ll take a weekend roughly once every six to eight weeks.

What We’re Looking For:

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience, including significant time building and owning distributed systems in production.
  • Strong production software skills, ideally in at least one object-oriented language. You write clean, tested code and can make targeted changes in large open-source codebases you didn’t write.
  • Deep understanding of distributed systems: performance, scaling and failure modes. You can reason about how a system will break before it does.
  • Experience running multi-tenant systems at scale on Kubernetes in AWS, GCP or Azure, with infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform, Helm or Jsonnet.
  • Hands-on experience designing and implementing SLOs.
  • Experience being on call for production systems. You troubleshoot calmly and methodically under pressure, and you’ve taken part in blameless incident response and written high-quality post-incident reviews.
  • Staff-level technical leadership: driving cross-team projects, setting technical direction and making the engineers around you better.
  • Working knowledge of Linux internals, networking and cloud storage.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience with Mimir, Loki, Tempo, Pyroscope, Prometheus or other observability and time-series databases.
  • Open-source contributions.
  • Customer reliability engineering (CRE) or customer-facing escalation experience.

In the UK, the Base compensation range for this role is £103,958 - £124,750. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed in the interview process. Benefits include equity, bonus (if applicable) and other benefits listed here.#LI-Remote

#LI-Remote

*Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process.

Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs:

  • 100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose.
  • Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment.
  • Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates.
  • Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things.
  • Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work.
  • Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics.
  • Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career.
  • Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human.
  • Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do.
  • In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it.
  • Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable.

Equal Opportunity Employer: Grafana Labs is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from everyone regardless of race, colour, nationality, origin, caste, sex, gender reassignment identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, religion or belief, disability, veteran status, genetic information, pregnancy, maternity, marital, family or carer status, or any other characteristic which is protected by local law. jobs.title: Events Lead, UK & International
jobs.description:
Events Lead, UK & International

Substack is building a new economic engine for culture, giving the brightest, most interesting and creative people on the internet the power of their own publishing platform. Substack empowers creators with financial autonomy, ownership and a direct connection to their communities. Substack’s model, based on direct subscriptions, has fueled an explosion of independent publishing and is revolutionizing culture.

 

We're looking for an Events Lead, UK & International to create and execute an exceptional year-round programme of events in the UK in service of our creators and our mission to be a new home of culture, and oversee the delivery of our growing calendar of events internationally too. This means you’ll devise the strategy, planning, and execution of Substack's brand events portfolio in the UK whilst simultaneously building the framework for our growing international activity, from flagship brand moments in London to intimate creator gatherings in Sydney.

 

You’ll create meaningful brand and creator events that are genuinely creative, unique and fun to attend, help foster our community of bestsellers and attract more people to join Substack, and show people they are part of something truly special by being part of our platform. You'll work at the intersection of culture, technology, and media, partnering with some of the most interesting voices shaping our world, across the ideological spectrum.

 

This role reports to the Head of Communications & Brand and is based in London.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Shape the strategy. Develop and execute a UK events strategy that advances Substack's brand and business goals in the UK, and ideate and oversee events in key territories internationally with the Head of International and country leads. Identify innovative opportunities to enhance our brand, drive cultural conversation, and attract new creators and subscribers.

  • Drive execution excellence. Manage the full event lifecycle in the UK—from concept and promotion through on-the-ground coordination —ensuring every detail reflects the quality and creativity of the Substack brand. You will also be responsible for ensuring that your events travel far and wide on social and in the press, as a key pillar of our brand marketing strategy.

  • Enable partnerships. Empower our Partnership Leads to bring market-specific event ideas to life, providing strategic guidance and operational support to ensure strong execution in key territories.

  • Manage resources strategically. Manage a UK events budget with clear goals, measurement frameworks, and ROI tracking, and build effective processes internationally. This includes building methodologies to demonstrate impact and communicate wins internally.

jobs.description:
Scientific Account Executive

Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

Weâre growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the role

This is a hybrid sales and customer success role for someone with real scientific depth. You'll be the primary point of contact for customers â from first conversation through ongoing engagement. That means understanding what a protein design team is actually trying to achieve, helping them pick the right assays, making sure their experiments are set up correctly, and translating results back into language that's useful for their programs.

The day-to-day:

  • Running technical sales calls where you discuss binding kinetics, expression systems, and assay design, not just pricing

  • Onboarding new customers and helping them design their first experiments on the platform

  • Monitoring ongoing accounts, flagging issues early, and proactively suggesting next steps based on their results

  • Working with the biology team to troubleshoot when a customer's experiment doesn't go as expected

  • Identifying expansion opportunities within existing accounts â new targets, new assay types, larger campaigns

You won't be handed a script. You'll need to understand the science well enough to earn trust from PhD-level protein engineers and CSOs, while also being commercially sharp enough to close deals and grow accounts.

Responsibilities

  • Own the full customer lifecycle: prospecting, technical sales conversations, deal closing, onboarding, and ongoing account management.

  • Serve as the technical point of contact for customers. Understand their protein engineering goals and recommend the right experiments (binding, expression, thermostability, enzyme activity).

  • Understand and explain our assay capabilities in depth: BLI, SPR, cell-free expression, and emerging assay types. Know when each is appropriate and what the data means.

  • Work closely with the biology team to ensure experiments are designed correctly and results are communicated clearly.

  • Build and maintain a pipeline of commercial opportunities across customer segments: AI-driven protein design companies, biotech startups, pharma R&D teams, and academic labs.

  • Develop proposals and quotes tailored to customer needs, from small pilot experiments to large-scale data generation campaigns.

  • Represent Adaptyv at conferences and industry events. Be able to have deep technical conversations at the booth, not just hand out brochures.

  • Feed customer insights back to the product and biology teams: what assays are people asking for, what's missing, where are we losing deals.

What we're looking for

  • Scientific background in protein engineering, biochemistry, biophysics, or a related field. You should be comfortable discussing binding kinetics (KD, kon, koff), expression systems, and assay design without needing to look things up.

  • Experience in a customer-facing technical role: field application scientist, technical sales, scientific account management, or similar. CRO or biotech vendor experience is a strong plus.

  • Commercially driven. You care about revenue, pipeline, and closing deals, not just having interesting scientific conversations.

  • Strong communicator who can adapt to the audience: detailed and technical with a scientist, concise and business-focused with a VP.

  • Self-starter who can manage their own pipeline and priorities without heavy oversight.

  • Genuine interest in AI-driven protein design and the companies working in this space. You follow what's happening in the field.

Application deadline

Lead Talent Partner - Product and Engineering

Orbital is the AI platform for real estate legal work.

Real estate shapes the world around us: our homes, our workplaces and our cultural landmarks. It’s the infrastructure that powers everyday life and is the world's largest asset class. Yet behind every single deal, real estate and legal teams work hard to navigate decades-old complexity; manually connecting documents, hidden obligations, geo-spatial context, and multiple parties into a path forward. We connect the legal and physical record, so that path is clearer than ever before. Our mission is to make real estate transactions faster, clearer, and less manual.

Here, you'll be part of changing how the deals behind the largest asset class get transacted, and will help shape the future of real estate.

A bit about us:

🚀 We’re building at the forefront of AI technology, without losing the deeply human expertise our clients depend on.

🏢 Orbital is built with former practising real estate lawyers and 250+ years of combined legal expertise. We're purpose-built for the complexity of real estate: accelerating due diligence, drafting and negotiation, and deal coordination with legal-grade precision.

💰 We've just raised a $60m Series B, led by Brighton Park Capital, to accelerate our global expansion – $75m raised to date.

🤝 We're trusted by 5,000+ real estate professionals, spanning UK Magic Circle and US Am Law 100 firms, to household names like M&S. Leading firms like BCLP, Orrick, Goodwin, Womble Bond Dickinson and Clifford Chance rely on Orbital to remove the busywork, freeing legal and real estate teams to focus on sharp judgment, standout client service, and closing deals faster.

💡 Working at Orbital means joining a bold, ambitious team, with the trust to take ownership and make a real impact from day one.

Orbital is entering a major scaling chapter, and Product Engineering + Design Engineering are at the heart of it. We’re looking for an exceptional Lead Talent Partner to own how we find, attract, engage, assess and close the very best Product Engineers and Design Engineers in a fiercely competitive market.

This is a low-volume, high-calibre role. Success looks like building a market-leading attraction engine and a repeatable hiring system that consistently delivers bar-raising hires, primarily in the UK (with occasional US roles).

The role, in a nutshell

You’ll be the CTO’s partner for Product & Design Engineering hiring — owning the strategy, the operating rhythm, and the market-facing plan that enables Orbital to repeatedly win top talent.

At Orbital, these roles are typically:

  • Product Engineers: product-minded full‑stack engineers who ship end-to-end customer value.

  • Design Engineers: frontend/UI engineers operating at the intersection of design and engineering, with high craft.

You’ll work closely with the CTO, senior Product/Engineering/Design leaders, and a marketing specialist to build the narrative, content and materials that help Orbital stand out — and convert the best people over time.

What you’ll do

1) Own the Product & Design Engineering hiring strategy (CTO partnership)

  • Build and own a forward hiring plan with the CTO/COO: forecasting, sequencing, and prioritisation.

  • Own the hiring plan and reporting in the ATS (e.g. Ashby): req pipeline, stage design, interviewer pools, and metrics.

  • Act as a trusted advisor to senior stakeholders on:

    • market intelligence and compensation benchmarks

    • org design and team build sequencing

    • interview plan quality and signal

    • funnel health and quality indicators

2) Build a market-leading attraction engine (content + community + creative search)

  • Design and run a high-touch, always-on engagement and nurture engine for top Product & Design Engineering talent (not tied only to live reqs).

  • Partner with leadership and marketing to create standout content and outreach materials (positioning, sequences, technical narratives, proof points, community activity).

  • Establish targets (set with the CTO) and report on pipeline health and learning loops:

    • warm pipeline size by discipline/level

    • engagement rates (reply / meeting booked)

    • nurture → active candidate → offer → accept conversion

    • competitive intel and drop-off reasons

3) Deliver hiring outcomes (low volume, very high calibre)

  • Personally own the most senior and business-critical Product Engineering hires (e.g., Staff/Principal/Lead level and key leadership roles).

  • Protect the quality bar for assessment, references, and offer calibration; step in on escalations and closing.

  • Set the operating rhythm: pipeline reviews, prioritisation, stakeholder alignment, and continuous improvement.

What we’re looking for (must-haves)

  • Scale-up experience: proven track record hiring in a high-growth tech scaleup with high standards and ambiguity.

  • Deep Product & Design Engineering market immersion: credible, active network in the UK. Ideally you have run meetups and build communities. You know who the standout people are and what motivates them.

  • Exec-search level craft: evidence of closing low-volume, very high-calibre engineers via creative, non-standard routes (not just inbound + job boards or Linkedin).

  • Attraction + nurture strategy: you’ve built always-on engagement motions that convert exceptional people over time (content, community, referrals, targeted events, high-touch outreach).

  • CTO partnership: you’ve partnered closely with technical leadership to define quality, design assessment, and calibrate the bar.

  • Strong written narrative and messaging: you can translate a technical story into compelling outreach/materials (and collaborate well with marketing).

  • Data-informed judgement: you use metrics as feedback loops for quality and funnel health — and can clearly explain what you track and why.

What this role is not (important)

  • Not high-volume recruiting — this is low volume, bar-raising hiring.

  • Not a “maintain the process” job — you’ll build and continuously improve the attraction engine and operating model.

  • Not fully remote — hiring is UK-first and roles are hybrid.

Working model & location

  • Location: London, UK 2-3 days a week.

  • Working model: Hybrid (all roles)

🔒 Security is everyone’s responsibility at Orbital. We ask all team members to follow our security policies, complete regular awareness training, and handle sensitive data with care in line with ISO 27001 standards. Spot something unusual? Reporting risks or incidents quickly helps us maintain the strong culture of security and compliance we all depend on.

💡 At Orbital, we’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We especially welcome applications from people who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. Even if you don’t meet every single requirement, or if the right role isn’t listed yet, we’d still love to hear from you.

💰 This hiring range is a reasonable estimate of the base pay range for this position at the time of posting. Pay is based on several factors, which may include job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and business requirements.

Everyone who works with Orbital goes through background screening before they start. It's part of how we keep Orbital secure, for the people who work here and for the client information we're trusted with.

Compensation: £85K – £107K

Head of Design

Orbital is the AI platform for real estate legal work.

Real estate shapes the world around us: our homes, our workplaces and our cultural landmarks. It’s the infrastructure that powers everyday life and is the world's largest asset class. Yet behind every single deal, real estate and legal teams work hard to navigate decades-old complexity; manually connecting documents, hidden obligations, geo-spatial context, and multiple parties into a path forward. We connect the legal and physical record, so that path is clearer than ever before. Our mission is to make real estate transactions faster, clearer, and less manual.

Here, you'll be part of changing how the deals behind the largest asset class get transacted, and will help shape the future of real estate.

A bit about us:

🚀 We’re building at the forefront of AI technology, without losing the deeply human expertise our clients depend on.

🏢 Orbital is built with former practising real estate lawyers and 250+ years of combined legal expertise. We're purpose-built for the complexity of real estate: accelerating due diligence, drafting and negotiation, and deal coordination with legal-grade precision.

💰 We've just raised a $60m Series B, led by Brighton Park Capital, to accelerate our global expansion – $75m raised to date.

🤝 We're trusted by 5,000+ real estate professionals, spanning UK Magic Circle and US Am Law 100 firms, to household names like M&S. Leading firms like BCLP, Orrick, Goodwin, Womble Bond Dickinson and Clifford Chance rely on Orbital to remove the busywork, freeing legal and real estate teams to focus on sharp judgment, standout client service, and closing deals faster.

💡 Working at Orbital means joining a bold, ambitious team, with the trust to take ownership and make a real impact from day one.

The role

You will report directly to the CTO and work alongside engineering, product, legal engineering and AI from the start. Your direct team is small today, three designers, and you will shape how it grows from here.

Your starting point is not a design backlog handed to you in advance. It is the product strategy, growth ambition, and AI-first operating model, and you will use that context to set the design agenda.

Orbital is at an inflection point. The product is live and trusted by some of the most demanding real estate legal professionals in the world. The challenge now is not building something from scratch but making it significantly better: cleaner, faster, and genuinely easier to trust. As the product scales across the UK and US, the design function needs to grow with it, and you will be the person who builds it.

What you'll do

Lead from the product.

Your first team is the product engineering leadership team. You will be part of product, commercial, and strategic conversations, bringing a strategic design perspective to business challenges rather than representing the design function in isolation. From there, you will form your own view on where the product experience is constraining growth, where the interface is creating friction for users, and what needs to change. You will help the leadership team pressure-test product decisions against user reality, spot where information architecture, interaction patterns, or visual clarity are becoming bottlenecks, and ensure that how we design is aligned with where the business is heading.

Set the design agenda from product context.

You will not be given a predefined project list. You will assess what you learn from the product, the users, and the business and set the design priorities from there. That means making sure areas like information architecture, interaction design, design systems, user research, and AI interface patterns are pointed at the right problems and prioritised accordingly. A major part of the brief is translating current product realities into a sharper design mandate and challenging existing assumptions when the evidence demands it.

Define what AI-native design looks like here.

The hardest design problems at Orbital are not aesthetic. They are epistemic. How do you help a real estate lawyer trust an AI output enough to put their name to it? How do you present the reasoning behind a 50-document analysis in a way that a partner can review in 20 minutes? How do you make agentic behaviour feel controllable to a professional who is accountable for the outcome? You will set the standard for how Orbital answers those questions, shape the interaction patterns that distinguish our product from everything else in the market, and hold the wider team accountable for the quality of the experience we ship.

Build the design function.

You will be the consistent presence the design team anchors around. Alternance - Commercial·e / Sales / Business Developer

Le département Sales compte une trentaine de personnes réparties entre la qualification des prospects et le closing. Leur objectif commun : accompagner les prospects jusqu’à la signature du contrat en Assemblée Générale.

Notre cycle de vente est long et complexe en BtoC (3 à 4 mois en moyenne). La particularité ? La copropriété doit voter à la majorité lors de son assemblée générale pour souscrire à notre solution.

En tant qu’alternant·e Sales Development Representative, tu es le premier point de contact et le premier maillon de notre chaîne commerciale. Ton rôle est stratégique : transformer l’intérêt d’un prospect en une opportunité commerciale réelle pour les Account Executives.

Il existe 600.000 copropriétés en France et chacune d’elle constitue une communauté à part entière, dont il nous faut comprendre le fonctionnement afin de les convaincre de nous rejoindre ! Nos prospects peuvent aussi bien être une petite copropriété de 3 lots en zone rurale, déjà autonome, qu’un grand ensemble immobilier de 300 logements en centre-ville, géré par un professionnel en face duquel nous présenterons une offre concurrente.

Tes missions en soutien de l'équipe Sales

En binôme avec nos commerciaux et sous la responsabilité de ton/ta manager, tu seras formé·e pour découvrir le métier de Sales Development Representative (SDR).

Tes missions consisteront à :

• Prendre en main la qualification : Réaliser les premiers échanges téléphoniques avec les prospects ayant formulé une demande de devis pour instaurer un premier contact de confiance.
• Comprendre les besoins : T'entraîner à analyser les problématiques rencontrées au sein des copropriétés et présenter les offres Matera.
• Assister les Account Executives : Participer à la prise de rendez-vous de démonstration et épauler les AE dans le suivi des prospects, la préparation des assemblées générales et les tâches administratives.
• Découvrir nos outils Sales : Participer à la tenue à jour de notre CRM (Hubspot) et appliquer les bonnes pratiques de suivi.
• Contribuer à l'amélioration continue : Proposer tes idées et participer aux projets internes visant à fluidifier nos processus commerciaux.

Ton parcours d'intégration & d'apprentissage :


• Deux semaines d'immersion : Découverte de nos métiers, de nos équipes et de notre vision globale.

jobs.title: Data Engineering & Analytics Manager
jobs.description:
Data Engineering & Analytics Manager

Insurance is a numbers business, and most of those numbers are harder to trust than they look. You would lead the team that defines the numbers Insify runs on, from the event a customer fires on our website to the report a risk carrier audits months later.


About the Role

You would lead our Data & Analytics team of 3-4 engineers end to end: ingestion, the warehouse and its models, the metric layer, and the analysis and reporting built on top of it. It is a small team with a big surface, so there is nowhere to hide and nothing you can't reach.

We are deliberately not splitting data engineering from analytics. At our size the hard problems sit in the handover between the two, and we want one person who enjoys that whole puzzle.

The team serves four groups with genuinely different needs. Growth wants hourly to daily signals and can live with approximately right. Carrier reporting and corporate finance are calendar-locked and need numbers that reconcile and survive an audit months later. Actuarial needs depth and lineage over speed. Prioritising here is arbitration between things that fail in different ways, and the arbitration is yours.

It's a hands-on role. You can open the warehouse and read the models, you review a new data model before it ships, and your team trusts your technical judgement because you still use it. The job is still the team: its own game, its communication, and each person in it. When something slips, hands-on work is the first thing that yields.


What you'll be doing
  • Leading a team of 3-4 data engineers and analysts end to end: what it builds, how it runs in production, and who you hire and grow to get there
  • Running discovery with the teams we serve: understanding what they need from data, and bringing the platform and datasets that enable them
  • Owning the trade-offs between Growth, carrier reporting, finance and actuarial: deciding what the team works on, driving alignment with key partners across other teams, and saying no when the answer is no
  • Making the platform scale: a new country, carrier or product should mean configuration and reused models, and recurring manual work, like carrier reporting and cash reconciliation, should turn into automation
  • Bringing engineering excellence to how the team works: data contracts with product teams, testing in CI, alerts that get resolved, a way to try changes before they hit production
  • Challenging our ideas and bringing your own. We encourage each other to act this way, so you can expect the same from others

    • What you'll need
  • You've managed or led a data team before, including hiring, feedback and growing people. It doesn't have to be for long, but it has to be real and you have to want more of it
  • Depth on one side of the data stack and working fluency on the other. You still love shipping, you review your team's work, and they trust your judgement on it
  • A track record of shaping what gets built, not only how: you've turned business problems into data priorities, cut scope, and can show the decisions that followed
  • Ownership & impact instinct - when needed you go beyond your team's boundaries to get to results
  • You get real leverage out of AI in your daily work, and you can say where it helped, and where it hurt. Your team gets that from you: you try new tools and ways of working first, and bring the ones that stick

    • Nice to have
  • Experience with reporting that has to reconcile: bordereaux, revenue, cash, ledger
  • Experience building B2B products, especially in insurance & fintech
  • Experience working on a product distributed across different country markets
  • Experience with Databricks, dbt and event tracking (Snowplow or similar)

    • Our stack

    Databricks with Unity Catalog, dbt with SQL-based transformation, running on AWS.

    None of this is a hard requirement, and you don't need to know all of our stack. We care more about how you reason about data, systems and teams than which tools you have used. Strong on most of it? Apply.


    How we hire
    Five conversations, each with a clear purpose, and you hear where you stand after every one:
    1. Leadership. We look at your experience with performance management, personal development and building teams.
    2. Data Model Review. You review a change to our warehouse models with two of our engineers.
    3. Data Platform Design. A modelling and platform problem close to what we deal with.
    4. Values Interview. We look at your approach to work, and how it adds to our Values.
    5. Meet the Founder.
    You get the outcome within three days of your last round, with specific feedback either way.
     

    We offer
  • Competitive compensation. We offer a salary in the range of 85k-110k EUR plus performance-based equity grants
  • Hybrid. 3 days in the office, 2 from home, up to 4 weeks a year from abroad, 25 holiday days
  • Pension. 6% employer contribution
  • Wellbeing budget. €50 net a month via Epassi, from the gym to takeaway, rolls over
  • Learning and coaching. Internal leadership programs and coaching
  • Central Amsterdam office. Shared lunches, dogs, Friday drinks, high-spec MacBook Pro

    • About Insify

    Insify is a high-growth scale-up backed by €43M in total funding from world-class investors like Accel, Munich Re Ventures, and Formula 1 champion Nico Rosberg. In five years, we've expanded from the Netherlands into France and Germany, and we're just getting started. Our mission: become the European leader in AI-powered SME insurance.

    We aren't just building a company; we're leading a revolution. Our culture is intense, high-stakes, and mission-driven. We hire smart, ambitious "owners" who possess a relentless drive to win. This is an environment for those who thrive on challenges, value intellectual honesty, and share our mindset of becoming a global category leader.

    Our founding team consists of seasoned entrepreneurs who have previously built iconic businesses like HelloFresh, Bloomon, and SumUp. We bring that same bias for speed, scale, and high standards to one of the most structurally broken experiences in financial services. Together, we combine that deep fintech and e-commerce expertise with cutting-edge AI to stay ahead of the curve.

jobs.title: Containerization & Virtualisation Engineer
jobs.description:
Containerization & Virtualisation Engineer

Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1000+ colleagues in 70+ countries and very few office based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.

The company is founder led, profitable and growing.

This is a general selection process for software engineers focused on virtualisation and container technology - from the kernel through userspace. Apply here if you are an exceptional Go, Rust, or C/C++ software engineer and want to work on next-generation open source VMM or container technology, or related open source networking and storage.

Container, virtualisation and cloud infrastructure have become essentials of modern software deployments. We invest in open source related to application isolation, workload orchestration, system or OCI containers, micro service architecture or cloud infrastructure.

Here are some examples of projects under way at Canonical.

RustVMM has great potential as a new hypervisor for Linux. We are building a team to work on this, with an emphasis on performance, security and operability. Work in Rust and bring your expert knowledge of VMM and related kernel networking and storage capabilities.

Docker images are easy to make and publish on Docker Hub and other registries, but the quality, consistency and security maintenance of those images is broadly very poor. Canonical is in a good position to publish a portfolio of outstanding Docker images. Our Rockcraft team is designing and implementing an elevated Docker image experience for the open source community.

LXD is a modern system container and virtual machine manager that is widely used on Ubuntu, ChromeOS and other Linux platforms. LXD engineering spans the entire software stack from low-level kernel work on namespaces, confinement, security, filesystems, VMMs and networking, to the high level management REST API and CLI.

Members of the Kubernetes product team build MicroK8s for on-rails K8s, and Charmed Kubernetes for more sophisticated integration. We work on K8s itself and on the operations tooling around it.

The OpenStack team deliver Charmed OpenStack, OVN / OVS and Ceph. This work brings cloud platform technologies to large-scale computing environments.

These teams hire system level C/C++, Golang, Rust and Python developers to work on security-critical, performance-critical and mission-critical code, focused on software delivery, containers, security, sandboxing, application orchestration and management. Our teams are motivated to have a meaningful impact on modern cloud computing technologies.

Location: we have remote container and virt engineering roles in every time zone.

What you will focus on

  • Design and specify new features, building consensus on approach
  • Engage with upstream communities in your area of expertise
  • Conduct security analysis and reviews to ensure defence in depth
  • Create and monitor performance benchmarks to optimise your product
  • Collaborate proactively with a distributed team
  • Write high quality code to create new features
  • Debug issues and produce high quality code to fix them
  • Review code produced by other engineers
  • Discuss ideas and collaborate on finding good solutions

What we are looking for in you

  • An exceptional academic track record from both high school and university
  • Undergraduate degree in Computer Science or STEM, or a compelling narrative about your alternative path
  • Drive and a track record of going above-and-beyond expectations
  • You have worked on open source virt or container tech
  • You have experience working in the kernel or very low level system
  • Professional written and spoken English
  • Experience with Linux (Debian or Ubuntu preferred)
  • Excellent interpersonal skills, curiosity, flexibility, and accountability
  • Passion, thoughtfulness, and self-motivation
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills
  • Result-oriented, with a personal drive to meet commitments
  • Ability to travel twice a year, for company events up to two weeks each

Additional skills we value

  • Performance engineering and security experience

What we offer you

We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognise outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus. We provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

  • Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person
  • Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year
  • Annual compensation review
  • Recognition rewards
  • Annual holiday leave
  • Maternity and paternity leave
  • Employee Assistance Programme
  • Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues
  • Priority Pass, and travel upgrades for long haul company events

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open source projects and the platform for AI, IoT and the cloud, we are changing the world on a daily basis. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Canonical has been a remote-first company since its inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future, and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.

jobs.title: Forward Deployed AI Lead
jobs.description:
Forward Deployed AI Lead

Caylent is an AI-first cloud services company that helps organizations turn ambitious ideas into meaningful business impact. As an AWS Premier Tier Services Partner and a charter member of Anthropic’s Claude Partner Network, we combine deep expertise in AWS, artificial intelligence, and Anthropic’s Claude platform to help customers modernize their technology, build intelligent products, and move AI from experimentation into production.

Our capabilities span generative and agentic AI, cloud migration and modernization, cloud-native application development, data and analytics, DevOps, managed services, security and compliance, and customer experience transformation. At Caylent, our people always come first.

We are a fully remote global company with employees in Canada, the United States and Latin America. We celebrate the culture of each of our team members and foster a community of technological curiosity. Come talk to us to learn more about what it means to be a Caylien!

About This Role

Caylent’s Anthropic Business Unit is a dedicated AI services practice built in partnership with Anthropic.

The Forward Deployed AI Lead is the strategic and architectural lead on AI engagements. Paired with a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) who handles hands-on implementation, you own the engagement arc: shaping AI strategy, designing operating models, mapping AI outcomes to business value, and guiding executive stakeholders through adoption. You lead the room — the FDE builds what you architect.

This is a cross-functional role. You engage across lines of business, not just engineering, connecting AI initiatives to the outcomes that matter to each part of the organization. Every engagement is anchored to Anthropic’s platform and focused on real AI adoption outcomes.

Your clients span PE portfolio companies, growth-stage software businesses, and enterprise organizations. You are the strategic face of Caylent from kickoff through handoff.

What You’ll Do

Strategy and Architecture

  • Own AI engagements end-to-end as the strategic lead, from discovery through executive handoff, partnered with an FDE who drives implementation
  • Run structured discovery across engineering, product, and business stakeholders to map organizational context, AI readiness, and strategic goals across lines of business
  • Design AI operating models that define how the organization adopts, governs, and scales AI. Not just within engineering, but across the business
  • Define AI outcome maps that tie initiatives to measurable business results: efficiency gains, revenue impact, risk reduction, and time-to-value
  • Lead AI maturity assessments and architect near-term and long-term adoption roadmaps aligned to Anthropic’s platform capabilities
  • Facilitate executive workshops and enablement sessions for audiences ranging from engineering teams to C-suite leaders
  • Deliver executive presentations to CTOs, VPs of Engineering, and line-of-business leaders covering current-state findings, ROI projections, and strategic recommendations
  • Direct FDE work on Claude Code tooling, prompt architecture, and workflow automation. You set the technical direction, the FDE executes

Client Relationship and Business Development

  • Identify expansion opportunities across lines of business. AI strategy work naturally surfaces adjacent needs in departments beyond the initial engagement
  • Shape follow-on scope throughout the engagement: by Week 1, you should have a working hypothesis for the next engagement; by the final on-site block, you present it
  • Build executive relationships that position Caylent as a long-term AI strategy partner, not a one-time vendor
  • Attend on-site for the final Catalyst block: readout, workshop, and executive presentation

Internal Contribution

  • Contribute reusable strategy frameworks, delivery artifacts, and methodology improvements back into the practice at engagement close
  • Lead AI strategy engagements spanning multiple teams, platforms, and business functions
  • Collaborate with FDEs to refine the architect-engineer delivery model and improve handoff patterns

What We’re Looking For

Required

  • 8+ years of software development or technical architecture experience across varied stacks, including hyperscaler environments
  • 3+ years in engineering leadership, technical consulting, solutions architecture, or a combination
  • Demonstrated ability to engage across lines of business. You can talk to a VP of Engineering about CI/CD and a COO about operational efficiency in the same week
  • Experience designing or advising on AI operating models, technology adoption strategies, or digital transformation programs
  • Hands-on familiarity with Claude Code or equivalent AI-assisted development tools — you don’t need to configure them daily, but you need to speak the language credibly and direct an FDE’s work
  • Certified Claude Architect
  • Experience running structured stakeholder interviews, discovery sessions, and facilitated workshops with both technical and business audiences
  • Strong executive communication: writing and presenting to CTOs, VPs of Engineering, and line-of-business leaders
  • Experience delivering professional services engagements, including scope management, deliverable ownership, and client advisory
  • Working knowledge of CI/CD pipelines, DevOps practices, and modern software development workflows

Preferred

  • Experience mapping AI initiatives to business outcomes (revenue, efficiency, risk, time-to-value) with executive-level ROI framing
  • Familiarity with PE portfolio company environments and board-level communication
  • Background in solutions architecture, platform engineering, or enterprise technology strategy
  • Experience with LLM prompt engineering, agentic AI workflow design, or AI product development
  • Direct experience with Claude Code’s extensibility model
  • Familiarity with SDLC maturity frameworks or workforce analytics (DORA, DevEx)
  • Experience designing and facilitating workshops for mixed audiences — engineers, product managers, and business stakeholders

Who Thrives Here

The Forward Deployed AI Lead who do well here are a specific profile:

  • Sat in the seat. You’ve led engineering teams or technology strategy inside a product company and understand the pressures executives navigate when adopting AI. Clients can tell.
  • Thinks across the business. You don’t stop at engineering. You see how AI impacts operations, product, and go-to-market — and you can have those conversations with the people who own them.
  • Knows when to slow down. You surface risks before committing to an approach. When the client’s definition of the work is wrong, you say so.
  • Closes the next engagement. The final week of a Catalyst is a conversion window. You treat it that way — and the cross-LOB relationships you’ve built give you multiple paths to expand.
  • Makes the methodology better. Every engagement teaches you something. You feed it back into the practice rather than keeping it in your head.
  • Earns trust at the executive level. You’re as comfortable presenting an AI operating model to a COO in the morning as reviewing prompt architecture with your FDE that afternoon.

This is a poor fit if you want someone else to handle the sales motion or prefer execution-only roles. You are accountable for both strategic delivery quality and account expansion.

Why This Team

  • Ground floor of something real: this BU is early, well-resourced, and anchored to Anthropic. You're writing the playbook, not inheriting one
  • Own the methodology: you are shaping how AI-DLC enablement gets delivered. Every engagement you run improves the one after it
  • Proximity to the market: your clients are PE portcos, enterprise engineering orgs, and Anthropic-referred customers at the frontier of AI adoption
  • Revenue upside: Forward Deployed AI Lead who drive account expansion earn on revenue generated, not just delivery margin
  • AI-native by default: this team uses AI in how it works. Specification-First Engineering is how we move from prototype to production fast
  • Outcomes, not hours: advancement tied to delivery performance and account growth, not utilization

Benefits

  • 100% remote work
  • Equitable Life - Hybrid Plan
  • 100% Premium Coverage for the employee and dependents
  • Competitive phantom equity

  • Paid for exams and certifications

  • State of the art laptop and tools

  • Work with an amazing worldwide team and in an incredible corporate culture

This role may require up to 50% travel, depending on business needs.

Base Salary Range: The expected base salary range for this position is CAD $228,000 - $253,000 per year, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

Additional Compensation Components: In addition to the base salary, the compensation package may include bonuses, commissions, equity, and other incentives. The specific components will vary depending on the role and individual and/or company performance.

jobs.title: Clinical Director, Clinical Development
jobs.description:
Clinical Director, Clinical Development

Clinical Director, Clinical Development

Position Summary

The Clinical Director, Clinical Development, leads the clinical and scientific aspects of one or more Natera-sponsored clinical studies and is accountable for study-level clinical data integrity and patient safety. This role contributes to broader program strategy while ensuring high-quality study execution within an established development framework.

The Clinical Director drives progress on defined assignments while anticipating challenges and proactively adjusting tactical direction in alignment with senior leadership. This individual serves as a key cross-functional partner, representing the clinical development perspective internally and externally, and plays an important role in advancing research and product vision.

Primary Responsibilities

Study Leadership & Clinical Oversight

  • Lead the clinical and scientific aspects of one or more Natera-sponsored clinical studies.
  • Ensure study-level clinical integrity, data quality, and patient safety.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional study team members to ensure successful adherence to study timelines and budget, and achievement of study milestones
  • May oversee the work of Clinical Scientists working on the same or related studies.
  • Contribute to program-level strategy in partnership with senior clinical leadership.
  • Analyze and interpret study data to identify emerging trends, inform decisions and mitigate risks.
  • Anticipate probable obstacles and implement appropriate changes in direction.
  • Provide clinical input into study design, protocol development, study execution, and data interpretation.
  • Establish and maintain productive relationships with clinical investigators and other key external stakeholders in support of the Natera-Sponsored study portfolio.

Strategic Contribution & Execution

  • Receive defined assignments from manager while effectively driving progress independently within established structures and communicating regularly on milestones and challenges.
  • Participate in establishing strategic plans, objectives, and tactics in partnership with manager and Clinical Development team.
  • Assess risks, analyze information and communicate trade-offs in order to facilitate decisions on goals and priorities.
  • Work on problems of moderate scope requiring evaluation of multiple variables and data sources.
  • Exercise sound judgment within defined procedures and practices, ensuring adherence to standard operating procedures and other quality standards for clinical research.

Cross-Functional & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Build productive relationships with cross-functional teams (e.g., Clinical Operations, Regulatory, Biostatistics, Safety, Medical Affairs).
  • Develop and maintain strong external investigator relationships.
  • Represent the clinical function in cross-functional meetings and project discussions.
  • Regularly interact with senior management as a representative of the clinical team.
  • Represent company and departmental interests with external stakeholders.
  • Lead or support partnership discussions by engaging with senior external leaders.
  • Identify and pursue opportunities to communicate research and product vision internally and externally.
  • Manage executive stakeholders independently within assigned projects.
  • Participate in limited regulatory interactions as appropriate.

Leadership & Team Development

  • May provide indirect supervision, coaching, or mentoring to professional individual contributors.
  • Serve as a resource to team members and support a collaborative, high-performing team culture.

Qualifications

  • MD (or equivalent medical degree) required.
  • Board Certification/Eligibility in Oncology & Hematology strongly preferred
  • 3 or more years of experience in vitro diagnostics, life sciences or pharmaceutical clinical development; OR 5 or more years post-graduate clinical trials or clinical research experience in the academic setting
  • Typically requires 3 or more years of medical monitoring experience
  • Demonstrated ability to work cross-functionally in a matrixed organization in order to measure study progress against plans, proactively communicate challenges and propose solutions.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Extensive knowledge of clinical trial design, protocol development, informed consent development, case report form construction, study conduct, statistical analysis, data interpretation and clinical study reporting.
  • Knowledge of GCP, ICH and applicable guidelines and regulatory requirements.
  • Ability to assess clinical data and identify safety or operational risks.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Effective written and verbal English communication skills.
  • Ability to influence stakeholders internally and externally.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • Developing stakeholder management capabilities.
  • Ability to work independently while aligning with broader strategic direction.

Primary Demands and Work Environment

  • Operates in a dynamic, cross-functional, matrixed environment.
  • Requires regular interaction with senior management and external investigators.
  • May require periodic travel for site visits, investigator meetings, partnership discussions, or scientific presentations.
  • Primarily office-based or hybrid environment with extended computer use.
  • Must be able to manage multiple study responsibilities while maintaining attention to detail and clinical rigor.

The pay range is listed and actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. jobs.title: Extrusion & Process Technician or Extrusion Engineer (m/f/d)
jobs.description:
Extrusion & Process Technician or Extrusion Engineer (m/f/d)

About Humify GmbH

Humify is an innovative start-up developing a novel technology to convert biomass into valuable humic substances. Our mission is to improve soil fertility, support sustainable agriculture, and contribute to long-term carbon storage.

We are a small, international team of scientists and engineers working to bring this technology from the laboratory to industrial production.

The Position

We are looking for a hands-on person to support the operation, maintenance, and optimization of our small-scale extrusion equipment for biomass conversion.

You will work directly with our engineers and scientists to prepare experiments, operate the extruder, modify equipment, and ensure that our experimental processes run safely and reliably.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys practical technical work, solving mechanical problems, and experimenting with new technologies.

Your responsibilities

  • Equipment operation: Set up, operate, monitor, and maintain a laboratory- or pilot-scale extruder for biomass processing.

  • Experimental support: Prepare biomass feedstocks, conduct extrusion trials, collect samples, and document results.

  • Equipment assembly and modification: Assemble, adjust, and improve mechanical components, feeding systems, screw configurations, and other process equipment.

  • Maintenance and troubleshooting: Identify and resolve mechanical and operational problems, perform routine maintenance, and minimize equipment downtime.

  • Process monitoring: Monitor operating parameters such as temperature, pressure, screw speed, feed rate, and material flow.

  • Workshop activities: Support the construction of prototypes, installation of sensors, and modification of experimental equipment.

  • Documentation: Record operating parameters, maintenance activities, and experimental observations.

  • Safety and organization: Maintain a safe, clean, and well-organized technical workspace.

What you bring

  • Professional background as an extrusion technician, process technician, chemical engineer, or a comparable qualification

  • Practical experience in extrusion technology and process engineering, ideally within the chemical or environmental sector

  • Strong analytical skills and a hands-on approach to problem-solving

  • Hands-on mentality, attention to detail, and an independent, solution-oriented working style

  • Willingness to work with different biomass materials and conduct experimental trials

  • Good communication skills in English

What We Offer

  • Work on an innovative technology with the potential to improve soil health and contribute to climate protection.

  • A practical, varied role with direct involvement in research and technology development.

  • Opportunities to learn extrusion technology, hydrothermal processing, and experimental equipment development.

  • Close collaboration with experienced engineers and scientists.

  • A small, international team with short decision-making processes.

  • Competitive salary and opportunities for professional development.

Humify values diversity and equal opportunities. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, including individuals with disabilities, and support the compatibility of work and family life.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Join Humify and help us develop the technology to transform biomass into valuable resources for sustainable agriculture.

jobs.title: Werkstudent Bewerbermanagement (mind. 15h/Woche)
jobs.description:
Werkstudent Bewerbermanagement (mind. 15h/Woche)

Wir haben ambitionierte Ziele.

Werde ein Teil davon.

Von 0 auf 40 Teammitglieder in fünf Jahren. Wir gehören als Mix aus Strategieberatung und Kreativagentur zu den am schnellsten wachsenden inhabergeführten Beratungsunternehmen Süddeutschlands und möchten unseren Weg auch in Zukunft erfolgreich fortsetzen.

Hinter unserem „wir“ steht dabei ein Kollektiv aus engagierten Persönlichkeiten, was vielseitiger nicht sein könnte. Von ehemaligen Unternehmensberatern renommierter internationaler Unternehmen wie Ernst & Young oder Porsche Consulting über kreative Designprofis und Content-Experten bis zur TikTok Influencerin oder dem studierten Videografen, wir sind in unseren Fähigkeiten unterschiedlich, haben aber doch eine große Gemeinsamkeit: den Anspruch, uns kontinuierlich weiterzuentwickeln und herausragende Ergebnisse für unsere Kunden zu erzielen.

Wenn du Lust hast, in einem dynamischen und gleichermaßen etablierten Unternehmen auf Wachstumskurs mitzuarbeiten und Teil eines jungen, ambitionierten und freundschaftlichen Teams zu werden, dann bist du bei uns genau richtig.

Aufgaben

Dein Part in unserem Team.

In dieser Rolle bist du ein zentraler Teil unseres Recruiting-Setups für mittelständische Kunden. Der Schwerpunkt liegt klar im Bewerbermanagement. Du sorgst dafür, dass Prozesse sauber laufen, Bewerbungen zeitschnell weitergeleitet werden und unsere Kunden schnell und strukturiert über eingehende Bewerbungen entscheiden können.

Deine Tätigkeiten im Überblick:

  • Du kümmerst dich um das administrative Bewerbermanagement für unsere Kunden

  • Du pflegst und schaltest Stellenanzeigen auf verschiedenen Portalen und Websites

  • Du bist im engen Austausch mit den Geschäftsführern oder verantwortlichen Personalern unserer Kunden

  • Du führst eine saubere Bewerberübersicht, trackst Status, hältst Timings nach und stellst sicher, dass nichts liegen bleibt.

  • Du kommunizierst professionell und verbindlich mit Kandidaten, schriftlich und telefonisch.

Qualifikation

Was wir uns von dir wünschen.

Wir interessieren uns vor allem für dich als Menschen und prüfen immer individuell, ob deine Erwartungen, deine Skills und dein Drive zu uns passen. Eigenschaften wie selbstständiges Arbeiten, Verantwortungsbewusstsein und Aufgeschlossenheit gegenüber Neuem solltest du dabei auf jeden Fall mitbringen.

Zusätzlich sind folgende Punkte für die Stelle relevant:

  • Du bist eingeschriebener Student und kannst mindestens 15 Stunden pro Woche arbeiten

  • Du hast Lust auf strukturierte, verlässliche Arbeit mit klarer Verantwortung im Tagesgeschäft

  • Du kommunizierst sauber, freundlich und professionell, auch wenn es schnell gehen muss

  • Du arbeitest sorgfältig und dir ist Genauigkeit wichtig

  • Du kannst unterhalb der Woche deine Arbeitszeit flexibel auf mehrere Tage verteilen

Benefits

Warum wir kein normaler Arbeitgeber sind.

Partnerships Lead, UK&I

Build something monumental for Healthcare!

At Tandem Health we’re reimagining healthcare by putting clinicians first. Our platform - designed by clinicians, for clinicians - is built on deep insight into real-world pain points, with intuitive medical notes and workflows that truly support patient care.

We’re a fast-scaling health-tech company backed by top investors and expanding globally. We move fast, stay curious, and believe building something that matters starts with an extraordinary team. If you're passionate about impact and innovation, we'd love to meet you!

About the Role

We are looking for an ambitious, commercially driven Partnerships Lead to build and scale Tandem Health's strategic partnerships across the UK. You will play a key role in accelerating our growth by identifying and securing high-impact partnerships across the healthcare ecosystem, including NHS organisations, private healthcare providers, hospital groups and healthtech platforms.

You'll own the full partnership lifecycle, from identifying opportunities and building senior relationships through to negotiating agreements, launching partnerships and driving commercial value. Working closely with our commercial, product and leadership teams, you'll help unlock new routes to market, expand our distribution and establish Tandem as a leading AI partner to UK healthcare.

What You Will Do

  • Own and execute Tandem's UK partnerships strategy, identifying the relationships and channels that will have the greatest impact on our growth.

  • Identify and secure strategic partnerships across the UK healthcare ecosystem, including NHS organisations, private healthcare providers, hospital groups and specialist clinic networks.

  • Develop relationships with EHR/EMR providers, digital health platforms and complementary technology businesses to unlock new distribution and integration opportunities.

  • Originate and manage partnership opportunities end-to-end, from initial outreach and business development through to commercial negotiations, contracting and launch.

  • Develop compelling partnership propositions and commercial models that create value for both Tandem and its partners.

  • Drive tangible outcomes from partnerships, including revenue generation, customer acquisition, clinician adoption and market expansion.

  • Work closely with sales, product, project delivery, medical operations and marketing teams to ensure successful implementation and maximise the value of strategic partnerships.

  • Represent Tandem at industry events and conferences, building our profile and network across the UK healthcare market.

  • Monitor market developments and identify new opportunities to strengthen Tandem's competitive position and accelerate growth.

What You Bring

  • Proven experience in strategic partnerships, ideally within healthcare, healthtech or enterprise technology.

  • Strong understanding of the UK healthcare landscape, including NHS structures, private healthcare and the wider digital health ecosystem.

  • An established network of relevant industry contacts, with the ability to build credibility and influence senior decision-makers.

  • Demonstrable track record of originating and closing complex, high-value commercial partnerships.

  • Experience developing partnership strategies, identifying new routes to market and creating scalable commercial opportunities.

  • Strong commercial acumen, including the ability to assess opportunities, develop business cases and negotiate sustainable agreements.

  • Excellent communication, negotiation and stakeholder management skills, with confidence engaging C-suite executives and senior healthcare leaders.

  • Genuine interest in AI, healthcare innovation and transforming how healthcare is delivered.

How to Apply

We adopt a continuous selection process, so please make sure to apply with your CV in English.

Our interview process consists of stages:

  1. Screening interview with Talent Acquisition

Benefits

  • 30 days/year of paid vacation

  • £800 wellness budget per year

  • Social and team-building activities (off-sites, after works, winter/summer parties)

  • An opportunity to make a real positive impact in the world of healthcare

  • Work with some of the best minds in AI, healthcare, and engineering.


We review our benefits packages on a regular basis and might modify our benefits from time to time.

At Tandem, we move fast, think big, and take ownership. We're a high-performing, diverse team with a shared drive to change the future of healthcare - and we’re just getting started.

Our culture is built on action, ambition, and learning. You'll be trusted to take the lead, challenge yourself, and make an impact from day one. We believe real growth happens when you're stretched, supported, and surrounded by smart, passionate teammates who want to win together.

Even though we’re spread across countries, we come together often in Sweden for team meetings, social events, and offsites - blending global reach with real human connection.

We hire for talent, potential, and attitude - valuing different backgrounds and fresh perspectives. Great ideas come from everywhere, and we’re building a team that reflects the world we want to change.

Tandem handles sensitive patient data and will conduct a background check before hiring any candidate.

jobs.title: Senior Data Engineer
jobs.description:
Senior Data Engineer

📈 Who We Are:

We are rebuilding the energy transaction, making it transparent and fair.

Our goal is to put power back where it belongs, in the hands of customers and to take on one of the most critical problems of our century, access to low cost electricity.

tem exists to fix a broken global energy market that’s long favoured legacy operators, intermediaries, and opaque pricing. Today’s electricity system was not designed for rapid decarbonisation, AI-driven efficiency or fair access for the actual users - businesses and generators.

We’ve built the first AI native transaction infrastructure to reinvent how electricity is bought, sold and priced. Our technology is designed to cut out the inefficient fees, automate complex market flows, and bring transparency and fairness to energy transactions at scale.

In late 2025, after extraordinary growth, we closed a $75 million Series B - led by Lightspeed Venture Partners with participation from Albion, Atomico, Allianz, Hitachi Ventures, Hitachi Ventures, Schroders Capital and others - positioning us for global expansion, deeper product innovation and category leadership.

We’re scaling internationally and building toward a future where AI-driven infrastructure is foundational to electricity markets worldwide.

Since launch, our modern utility product, known as RED, has already facilitated thousands of business customers and billions in energy transaction value, proving that modern software and AI can transform an industry built on legacy systems.

At tem, we’re not just building another energy company, we’re rearchitecting market infrastructure so that transparency, efficiency and sustainability become the default, not the exception.

The Role

We're hiring a Senior Data Engineer.

Data sits at the core of what tem does. Our time-series data is the spine that runs from pricing through to billing: every transaction depends on it working. You'll be working across a genuinely varied set of workloads: textual data, time-series data, and event streams, each with its own ingestion and reliability challenges, including TSDS.

You'll join our Data Service team of 4, owning the design, reliability, and recovery strategy of specific ingestion pipelines and systems end-to-end. This is an individual contributor role: no team to manage, full ownership of the work you do. The team has more work than hands right now, and this role exists to close that gap so the business can move faster on the data it depends on.

You'll also work closely with our AI initiatives as they grow: the platform you own increasingly becomes the foundation those efforts depend on.

You will:

  • Own the design, reliability, and recovery strategy for the ingestion pipelines and systems in your domain.

  • Maintain and improve the data platform, including working through the existing tech debt backlog.

  • Build monitoring and alerting so issues surface before they become incidents.

  • Set the data quality checks that make an SLA commitment possible, and hold the line on them.

  • Help take the number of data products with a defined SLA from 2 to 10.

Responsibilities

Data Ingestion

  • Own the design, reliability, and resilience of ingestion pipelines end-to-end, including TSDS, with a clear recovery strategy when things break.

  • Build and maintain ETL/ELT pipelines for new and existing data sources.

  • Decide the right approach (batch vs. streaming) for each pipeline in your domain, including high-scale, low-latency requirements for time-series data.

  • Set data quality checks that make an SLA commitment possible, and hold the line on them.

Platform Maintenance

  • Own the day-to-day reliability of the data platform: monitoring, testing, and fixing issues before they become firefights.

  • Own code quality and standards for the systems you're responsible for, including CI checks (linting, tests, coverage).

  • Work through the existing tech debt backlog, prioritising fixes that unblock SLA commitments.

  • Optimise pipelines for performance and cost as data volumes grow.

  • Handle the failure modes specific to energy data: late arrivals, reprocessing, backfills.

Monitoring & Alerting

  • Build and improve observability across your systems so problems surface before they cause downstream impact.

  • Set up alerting tied to the SLAs the team is committing to.

  • Investigate and resolve issues within your domain, escalating genuinely cross-system problems.

Supporting Expansion

  • Help scope and prepare the platform for new data sources tied to international expansion.

  • Flag where current architecture won't hold up as scope grows, even if fixing it isn't your call to make alone.

  • Work closely with the AI team as their data needs on the platform grow.

Requirements

Must haves

  • Strong Python skills, with proven experience building and maintaining production data pipelines.

  • Experience owning the design, reliability, and resilience of a data pipeline or system end-to-end, not just writing pipeline code.

  • AWS or GCP experience.

  • Great communication skills, comfortable working directly with stakeholders to scope and agree SLAs, and explaining technical trade-offs to non-technical audiences.

  • Strong team player, comfortable working independently against a backlog and making judgement calls on prioritisation, while fitting into an existing team of 4.

  • Terraform experience.

Bonus points

  • Experience with time-series data at scale.

  • Experience with modern data stack tooling (Airflow, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, ClickHouse).

  • Experience in energy or climate tech.

  • Background in high-growth startups or scale-ups.

  • Genuine interest in how AI tooling and workflows intersect with data engineering.

We're open to someone who doesn't tick every box here, as long as they bring solid AWS or GCP experience and the ability to own their own work end-to-end.

Benefits & Perks

  • Salary aligned to internal benchmarks and reviewed twice a year.

  • Stock options so everyone has ownership in our mission.

  • 25 days holiday plus public holidays. Swap public holidays for the ones that matter most to you, and enjoy your birthday off.

  • Remote first and flexible working, with clear core hours and no internal meetings on Friday afternoons.

Home working and wellbeing budgets:

  • Up to GBP1,200 or EUR1,200 per year for your remote setup.

  • Up to GBP150 or EUR150 per month for wellbeing.

Interview Process

We move fast. Most processes take 2 to 3 weeks from first chat to offer. If you need us to adapt anything, let us know.

  • Intro call with Talent, 30 minutes.

  • Behavioural interview, 60 minutes.

  • Skills interview with cross-functional leaders, 60 to 90 minutes, including a practical exercise.

  • Bar Raiser interview with leadership stakeholders, 45 minutes.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities, including those that are traditionally underrepresented in the tech and energy sectors. If you’re excited about this role but not sure you meet every requirement, we’d still love to hear from you. Your unique perspective could be exactly what we’re looking for.

Machine learning is at the heart of Rosso, combining forecasting, optimisation and classical ML to process billions of data points and drive thousands of automated decisions a day. Every inference shapes the prices our customers see, so you can immediately see the impact of your work.

We have proved the concept with MVPs and POCs to grow to 2% of the UK market. Now we want to take it to the next level and build towards a state of the art solution, to fuel our expansion in the UK and take Rosso international.

We're looking for a Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineer to lead pricing ML within Rosso, building a platform that proactively drives growth by targeting the right customers to sign at the right time. The right person is energised by the greenfield environment: comfortable taking on ambiguity and able to make progress before the path is fully defined. They have built pricing, trading or optimisation systems that worked, ideally in energy or another market-driven domain, and have learned from the times they haven't. They'll bring that hard-won judgment to a system where the foundations are still being laid, and where early decisions compound. Success will be turning our current reactive system into a pricing engine which proactively drives growth by targeting the right customers to sign at the right time.
